root_cause.text: The `nau8821` audio codec driver fails to cancel or synchronize its pending delayed jack detection work (`jdet_work`) during component removal, allowing the work to execute after the driver module has been unloaded and causing a kernel crash.
root_cause.evidence: The patch resolves the issue by adding the `nau8821_component_remove` callback to `nau8821_component_driver` to invoke `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&nau8821->jdet_work)`, and the CVE description states that "Attempting to unload the driver while a jack detection work is pending would likely crash the kernel when it is eventually scheduled for execution".

bic_trace_step.reason: The driver initializes `jdet_work` in `nau8821_enable_jack_detect` (line 1649) and schedules it in `nau8821_interrupt` (line 539). However, in `nau8821_i2c_remove` (lines 1675-1682), it only frees the IRQ using `devm_free_irq` and does not cancel or synchronize the pending `jdet_work` work item. There is also no `.remove` callback in `nau8821_component_driver` (lines 1618-1636) to handle this cleanup, which leads to the described kernel crash when the module is unloaded while work is pending.
